title: Chinese ufology after Mao and the Falun Gong crackdown

tellings.quote: everything revolves around the the death of Mao Zong in 1976.

plain: A UFO historian named Richard Dolan, on Jesse Michels' podcast, describes how the study of UFOs grew in China after the death of the country's leader Mao Zedong in 1976, drawing on the writer Paul Dong. According to Dolan, everything turns on Mao's death, which opened room for the subject, until the government's 1999 crackdown on Falun Gong, a spiritual movement, closed it down again. If true, it shows a whole country's interest in UFOs rising and falling with its politics.
